h1: New York to Georgia car shipping
heroSub: About 850 to 950 miles, 2 to 3 days on the truck. Atlanta is where carriers reload, so pickups are easy to get and delivery into the metro is cheaper than almost anywhere else in the South.
intro:
New York to Georgia car shipping is a strong lane for one reason above all: Atlanta is a hub. Carriers coming down from the Northeast unload in the metro, reload with cars headed to Florida, Texas, or back north, and keep moving. That turnover means a car from the NYC area to Atlanta gets picked up fast and delivered for $650 to $750 on an open carrier, with 2 to 3 days in transit.

This guide covers the routes, the Atlanta neighborhoods where deliveries land, how the other Georgia cities price, who is moving, and two things people underestimate: Atlanta traffic and Georgia heat. Our thirteen New York offices all book Georgia; North Hempstead and the Bronx send the most. Use the quote tool beside this page for a live rate.

sections.h2: Three ways into Georgia: I-85, I-26 to I-20, and I-95 to Savannah
sections.html:
A carrier leaving the five boroughs or Long Island takes the Turnpike and I-95 to Richmond. For Atlanta, the common route then follows I-85 through Durham, Greensboro, and Charlotte into Georgia near Lavonia and down to the Perimeter, about 880 miles from Manhattan. Some drivers stay on I-95 to Columbia, then take I-26 to I-20 west through Augusta.

Savannah is a straight I-95 run of about 820 miles. Augusta is on I-20 off I-95 at Columbia. Macon and Columbus usually come off an Atlanta load, and Athens is 70 miles east of Atlanta off I-85. Carriers out of Schenectady and Albany often use I-81 instead. On-truck time is 2 to 3 days from any New York origin; pickup windows run 1 to 3 days.

sections.h2: Atlanta as a reload hub, and what it does to New York to Georgia car shipping prices
sections.html:
Most long-haul car carriers work a loop. A driver who leaves New Jersey with a mixed load for the Carolinas and Georgia drops the last cars in the Atlanta metro, then picks up cars bound for Florida, Alabama, Texas, or back up I-85.

For a New York customer this means two things. Trucks heading to Atlanta are plentiful, so pickup dates are easy to get and expedited pickup is rarely needed. And delivery inside the metro sits at the bottom of the Georgia range, typically $650 to $700 for a sedan, because the driver is going there anyway. Small-town Georgia is different. A delivery to Valdosta, Tifton, Dalton, or Brunswick takes the truck off the loop, and the price climbs $75 to $150 with a longer wait.

sections.h2: Buckhead, Midtown, Alpharetta, Marietta, and where cars land
sections.html:
Where in Atlanta matters for the handoff more than the price. Buckhead and Midtown are dense: high-rises, narrow side streets, and parking decks a hauler cannot enter. Drivers meet at a surface lot off Peachtree Road or Piedmont Road, or at a big-box store near the connector.

North of the Perimeter it gets easy. Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, Roswell, and Alpharetta have wide subdivision streets, and the Avalon and Windward areas are among the most common delivery points on this lane. Marietta, Kennesaw, Lawrenceville, and Duluth are the same story. Peachtree City has some truck-restricted streets, so the driver may plan a nearby lot. The door-to-door car shipping page explains how unreachable addresses are handled.

sections.h2: Savannah, Augusta, Macon, Columbus, and Athens
sections.html:
Savannah is the second most common Georgia destination. The Port of Savannah is also where cars leave the country. If you are shipping overseas, we handle the domestic leg from New York to the port or the freight forwarder's yard, and the ocean carrier takes it from there.

Augusta is home to Fort Eisenhower, the former Fort Gordon, and Columbus has Fort Moore, the former Fort Benning. Both get steady military moves with an off-base handoff; the military car shipping page covers orders and POV rules. Both price $50 to $100 above Atlanta. Athens is the University of Georgia, with move-in the second week of August and move-out in early May; the usual meeting point is a shopping center on Atlanta Highway.

sections.h2: Who uses New York to Georgia car shipping: Delta, Home Depot, Coca-Cola, and film crews
sections.html:
Corporate relocations lead the list. Delta is headquartered by the airport, Home Depot in Vinings, and Coca-Cola in Midtown, and all three move people from the Northeast with packages that typically cover one vehicle. Relocation coordinators usually book 2 to 4 weeks ahead, which keeps the pickup date certain.

Georgia Tech in Midtown and Emory in Druid Hills draw graduate students and faculty every August. The film industry is the newer driver. Studios in Fayetteville, Doraville, and Covington hire crews on three- to nine-month contracts, and schedules shift, so those customers often need a pickup on short notice; hub density makes that workable within 1 to 3 days. For most of these moves an open carrier is the right call.

sections.h2: Atlanta traffic, I-285, and when to schedule delivery
sections.html:
Atlanta traffic is a real factor in delivery timing. I-285 and the Downtown Connector, where I-75 and I-85 merge, are congested from about 6:30 to 9:30 in the morning and 3:30 to 7 in the evening, and worse in rain. Drivers do inside-the-Perimeter deliveries midday.

The driver will call the night before with a window of a few hours, and that window can shift if the Connector locks up. Keep the day flexible if you can; if you need a fixed time, say so at booking so dispatch places your car first on the route.

sections.h2: Summer heat and what to leave out of the car
sections.html:
From May through September a car on an open carrier in Georgia sits in direct sun at 95 degrees or more, and the cabin can pass 140. Anything that melts or bursts should come out before pickup: aerosols, lighters, candles, electronics, chocolate, wine, cosmetics. Cargo insurance does not cover personal items, so the car shipping checklist rule of leaving the car empty applies with extra force.

Make sure the battery is healthy and coolant is full, since the car is started several times during loading. Afternoon thunderstorms are normal, so a car may arrive wet and dusty; that is cosmetic, and the delivery inspection is still done against the pickup report. Enclosed solves both the sun and the rain.

faqs.q: How much is New York to Georgia car shipping for a regular sedan?
faqs.a: A running mid-size sedan on an open carrier to the Atlanta metro is typically $650 to $750. Savannah, Augusta, Athens, and Macon fall in the same range or slightly above. Small towns off the interstate loop add $75 to $150. Add $100 to $250 for an SUV or pickup, and 30 to 50 percent for enclosed transport.

faqs.q: How long does it take to ship a car from New York to Atlanta?
faqs.a: Expect 1 to 3 days for the truck to pick up after your first available date and 2 to 3 days on the road. Most cars are delivered within five or six days of booking. The hub traffic through Atlanta keeps pickups frequent, so even short-notice moves usually work without paying for expedited service.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to a high-rise in Buckhead or Midtown?
faqs.a: The truck cannot enter a parking deck or stop on a narrow side street, so the driver will arrange to meet you at a nearby surface lot, usually off Peachtree Road, Piedmont Road, or near a big-box store by the connector. The inspection and signature happen there and you drive the last few blocks.

faqs.q: Do you ship cars to the Port of Savannah for overseas transport?
faqs.a: Yes, for the domestic leg. We move the car from your New York address to the port terminal or the freight forwarder's receiving yard in Savannah or Garden City. You or your ocean carrier handle the export booking and customs paperwork. Send us the booking reference and the yard's receiving hours so the driver can deliver without a wait.

faqs.q: Is it safe to ship a car on an open carrier in a Georgia summer?
faqs.a: Yes. Open transport is how most cars reach Georgia year-round. The heat matters for what you leave inside, not the car itself, so remove electronics, aerosols, and anything that melts. Keep the battery and coolant in good shape since the car is started several times during loading. Enclosed transport is available if you want shade and rain protection.
